findings.highlight: He's prone to be misunderstood, yet he neither dabbles in relationships nor he does what typical students do for fun.
findings.evidenceJa: 誤解されやすいのだが、本人は色恋沙汰には手を出さないし、学生らしい遊びもしない。
findings.governingReading: Issei neither involves himself in romance nor plays in the manner of ordinary students.
findings.explanation: The paired neither-nor construction is ungrammatical.

findings.highlight: "I see. Hey, hand me the flathead screwdriver. The biggest one. Oh, and give me some conductors too. Yeah, this one looks salvageable."
findings.evidenceJa: 「そうか。—あ、マイナスドライバーくれ。一番おっきいヤツな。あと導線も。……うん、これぐらいならなんとか」
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks Issei for the largest flathead screwdriver and conducting wire.
findings.explanation: Electrical wire becomes plural conductors.

findings.highlight: "And you're saying that there's no room in the budget. ...Well, this one's just corroded. Good thing the inside's still intact."
findings.evidenceJa: 「けど予算にそんな余裕はない、と。……やっぱり劣化してるだけだな。中がイカレてなくて助かった」
findings.governingReading: Shirou determines that the current appliance is merely deteriorated and is relieved the inside is not ruined.
findings.explanation: General degradation becomes corrosion.

findings.highlight: The wires just burnt out, so as long as those get replaced, this should last until the end of the year."
findings.evidenceJa: 配線系のショートだから新しいのに替えれば、とりあえず今年いっぱいは頑張ってくれる」
findings.governingReading: The problem is an electrical-wiring short; replacing the relevant wiring should keep the heater working through the year.
findings.explanation: A short circuit becomes burned-out wires.

findings.highlight: "...There are two places where the wire's about to break... The electrical pipes should last a bit longer... The power cord should be fine with just insulation tape..."
findings.evidenceJa: 「……電熱線が断線しかかってるのが二つと……電熱管はまだ保つな……電源コードの方は絶縁テープでなんとかなる……」
findings.governingReading: Two heating wires are close to breaking, the heating tube or element still has life, and the power cord can be handled with insulation tape.
findings.explanation: Heating elements or tubes become electrical pipes.

findings.highlight: Had that been the case, a certain "Strengthening" would have to be done, which no amateur could manage, but I should be able to fix this one by sight.
findings.evidenceJa: その時は素人じゃない方法で“強化”しなくてはいけなかったが、これなら内部を視るだけで十分だ。
findings.governingReading: If the heating element were broken Shirou would need non-amateur Strengthening, but in this case merely seeing the interior is sufficient to diagnose before ordinary repair.
findings.explanation: Diagnosing by internal sight becomes repairing by sight.

findings.highlight: According to my old man, the fact that I can visualize objects' structures isn't really helpful.
findings.evidenceJa: 親父曰く、物の構造を視覚で捉えている時点で無駄が多い。
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu says that apprehending an object's structure visually already involves too much waste or unnecessary process.
findings.explanation: An excessively roundabout perceptual method becomes an unhelpful ability.

findings.highlight: That's why reading blueprints is a waste of time, and even that only helps seek out areas for magical energy to pass through.
findings.evidenceJa: だから設計図なんてものを読みとるのは無駄な手間だし、読みとったところで出来る事といったら魔力の通りやすい箇所が判る程度の話。
findings.governingReading: Even after reading the blueprint, the main gain is knowing which parts readily conduct magical energy.
findings.explanation: Recognizing mana-permeable locations becomes seeking places for mana to pass.

findings.highlight: I turn to face her, since she's been standing there the whole time.
findings.evidenceJa: ぼう、と立ったままの遠坂に振り返る。
findings.governingReading: Shirou turns back toward Rin, who is still standing blankly or absentmindedly, before greeting her and following Issei.
findings.explanation: The English preserves Rin standing there but drops her blank, distracted manner. The passage does not establish why she is in that state.

findings.highlight: "You made it just in time. Sorry for all the trouble, Emiya. I'm a bad friend for asking a favor from you and making you late for class."
findings.evidenceJa: 「ギリギリ間にあったか。すまんな衛宮、また苦労をかけた。頼み事をした上に遅刻させては友人失格だ」
findings.governingReading: Issei says he would fail as a friend if, after requesting help, he also made Shirou late.
findings.explanation: Issei's concern about what would make him a bad friend becomes an admission that he made Shirou late, even though they arrived in time.

findings.highlight: "What's with all the commotion so early in the morning, Emiya? Didn't realize you became Ryudou's whipping boy after you quit our club. Not that I care, but since you have no principles of your own, don't do anything to ruin our rep."
findings.evidenceJa: 「朝から騒がしいね衛宮。部活を辞めてから何をしてるかと思えば柳洞の太鼓持ち？　僕には関係ないけどさ、うちの評判を落とすような事はしないでよね。君、なんていうか節操ないからさ」
findings.governingReading: Shinji derides Shirou as Ryudou's flatterer or toady after leaving the club.
findings.explanation: Shinji's insult changes Shirou from Issei's toady into his victim or scapegoat. This alters the sneer, not the established facts of their friendship.

findings.highlight: "I'm not saying that. Just that I'm not involved and all. I'm not a part of the club anymore, so it's not right for me to just drop into the dojo.
findings.evidenceJa: 「興味じゃなくて用だよ。部外者なんだからおいそれと道場に行くの、ヘンだろ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou corrects Shinji: it is not that he lacks interest in the kyudo club, but that as an outsider he has no business casually entering the dojo.
findings.explanation: Shirou's explicit interest-versus-business correction disappears.

findings.highlight: "Fool, of course I'm concerned. You have a short fuse. Now granted, if you punched Shinji, that would've gotten you some applause, but it probably wouldn't make the girls happy. It wouldn't be right for me to put my friend in such an unpleasant position."
findings.evidenceJa: 「たわけ、心配もするわ。衛宮はカッとなりやすいからな。慎二に殴りかかれば皆は喝采を送るが、女どもからは非難の嵐だ。友人をそんな微妙な立場に置くのはよろしくない」
findings.governingReading: Issei predicts applause if Shirou hits Shinji but a storm of criticism from the girls.
findings.explanation: A storm of condemnation from the girls becomes their probable unhappiness.

findings.highlight: Probably nobody's thrilled by the idea of taking a teacher to the infirmary.
findings.evidenceJa: いい加減、担任を保健室に連れて行く、なんて慣習は打破したいと思っているのではなかろうか。
findings.governingReading: After a year with Taiga, the students presumably want to abolish the established custom of carrying their homeroom teacher to the infirmary.
findings.explanation: The class wanting to break its teacher-to-infirmary custom becomes generic reluctance.

findings.highlight: "Th-that's more like a threat! The moment the Tiger becomes the head of the baseball team, we'll all bound for the big Koushien tournament."
findings.evidenceJa: 「や、やめろよなそういう脅しは……！　タイガーが顧問になった日にゃ、オレたち甲子園いっちまうぞ！？」
findings.governingReading: A student fears that making Tiger the baseball adviser would take the team all the way to Koshien.
findings.explanation: The Koshien threat is grammatically incomplete.

findings.highlight: "Keep going! It's the punishment of the tiger!"
findings.evidenceJa: 「よし続けろ！　ガコロウトンの計じゃ！」
findings.governingReading: The student calls for the ガコロウトン stratagem; the source preserves an opaque named plan whose external reference is not established here.
findings.explanation: An unidentified named stratagem is invented as 'the punishment of the tiger.'

findings.highlight: Everyone must be on edge, since midterm tests are approaching.
findings.evidenceJa: 期末試験が迫ってきているんで、みんなてんぱっていたんだろう。
findings.governingReading: The narrator guesses the students are wound up because final exams are approaching.
findings.explanation: Final examinations become midterms.

findings.highlight: "You need to Tiger up!"
findings.evidenceJa: 「先生、起きないとタイガーです！」
findings.governingReading: Students shout that if the teacher does not wake she is Tiger, and that waking would be precisely what makes her Tiger.
findings.explanation: The escalating Tiger chant's deliberately broken predicates are normalized into slogans.

findings.highlight: When Fuji-nee says she gets mad, she gets mad. Doesn't matter if it's with a teacher or a student.
findings.evidenceJa: 藤ねえは怒るといったら怒る人だ。相手が生徒だろうが自分が教師だろうが関係ない。
findings.governingReading: When Taiga says she will get angry, she follows through regardless of the other person being a student and regardless of her own position as teacher.
findings.explanation: Taiga ignoring the teacher-student status difference becomes anger directed at either teachers or students.

findings.highlight: I was asked to help restock some product for a bar, since they wanted as many strong helping hands as they could get.
findings.evidenceJa: 飲み屋の棚卸しで、とにかく男手は多いほどいいから手伝いに来られるのなら来てほしい、という物だった。
findings.governingReading: The bar asks for help with 棚卸し, an inventory or stocktaking operation where more male labor would help.
findings.explanation: Taking inventory at a bar becomes restocking products.
